answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active association worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying on the reserve spaces, draws 8 Zoo cards and keeps 4 (discarding 4), and draws 2 Final Scoring cards. Place Animals side I in slot 1 (strength 1); place the other four side-I Action cards randomly in the remaining slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, 1 for second, 2 for third, and 3 for fourth.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C3: one active worker and remaining 3 lying down; D: 25 money; E: draw 2 Final Scoring cards; F: draw 8, keep 4, discard 4. B places Animals under leftmost slot and other four randomly, side I. C1 staggers Appeal 0–3 by turn order.

answers.answer: Setup places 3 face-up Base Conservation Projects for 2- or 3-player games, and 4 for a 4-player game. In a 2-player game only, block one level on each of the three face-up base projects (left on the left card, middle on the middle card, right on the right card) and the three donation spaces in the donation area's left column; these are blocked for both players. No blocked spaces are specified for 3- or 4-player games. Reveal the six-card display only after everyone has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c specifies 4 projects in a 4-player game, otherwise 3, and lists the 2-player blocked project levels and donation spaces. Setup G says reveal the display after everyone chooses hand cards.

answers.answer: After using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards from slots 1–3 one slot to the right, and put the used card in slot 1. Set action strength before performing the action. Each X-token spent adds 1 strength and returns to supply; X-tokens gained during that action cannot boost it. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. Resolve an 'after finishing' effect only after completing the action, including moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove the used card, shift all cards left of the empty slot right, and place the used card in slot 1. X-tokens set strength before the action and add +1 each, with a five-token holding limit. 'After finishing' effects follow the card move.

answers.answer: You may not take a regular action that does nothing (such as playing zero animals or building zero buildings). The alternative is to select an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; move that card to slot 1 and shift the intervening cards right. Its strength and upgrade side do not matter. You cannot take this action if you already have 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says you may not do nothing and directs players to the alternative X-token action. The X-token action gives exactly 1, moves the selected card to slot 1 regardless of strength or upgrade, and is unavailable at 5 tokens.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore further movement and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. The break occurs after that player's current turn is complete. After the break, return the token to its starting space; normal play continues clockwise with the next player, who takes the next turn.
answers.evidence: The Break track section says the break takes place after the current turn, the player gets 1 X-token, additional steps are ignored, and after the break the token resets.

answers.answer: On Cards I, first advance the Break token 2 spaces, then either draw from the deck according to the strength table (up to 3 cards, with a discard where indicated), or at strength 5+ snap exactly 1 display card of any reputation; snapping is not a deck draw. On Cards II, also advance the Break token 2, then draw from the deck and/or from display cards within reputation range in any order per the upgraded table; the display is not replenished until the turn ends. Cards II can snap exactly 1 display card at strength 3+, regardless of reputation, with no deck draw. Hand size is unlimited during a turn and enforced at breaks (normally 3, or 5 with the relevant university).
answers.evidence: CARDS action specifies 2 Break spaces on both sides, the side-I deck-or-snap choices, side-II deck/range draw and snap threshold, and end-of-turn display refill. Break procedure enforces the hand limit.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action; Cards II enables progress past 9. At reputation 15, further reputation stays at 15 and converts to 1 Appeal per remaining reputation step. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display defines range as the matching folder and lower-numbered folders, says 10+ requires upgraded Cards, and converts overflow at 15 to Appeal. It also says the discard pile may not be inspected.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building, with size no greater than action strength; Build II can build multiple different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but never two identical buildings in the same action. Pay 2 money per space, separately before placing each building. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; each later building must touch an existing building by an edge. Build only on empty spaces and do not extend off-map, overlap, or cover water/rock. Spaces with the restricted icon require Build II. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately grants 1 Appeal once.
answers.evidence: BUILD action gives the one-building/total-size limits, cost, ordinary placement restrictions, border rule for the first building, adjacency rule, restricted spaces, kiosk spacing, and pavilion Appeal.

answers.answer: Build I can build standard enclosures of size 1–5, kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo per zoo (size 3). Build II additionally permits a Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary (each size 5); each zoo may have at most one of each special-enclosure type. The supply has four tiles of each special enclosure for the four players. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 Appeal (with Build II needed to access restricted-icon spaces, though other effects can also complete the coverage).
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build lists the enclosures and per-zoo maxima; the text says four tiles of each special enclosure, unique buildings only via Sponsors, and a fully covered map grants 7 Appeal.

answers.answer: Bonuses gained earlier in an action—including money, cards, and newly activated workers—may be used for later steps of that same action. Pay for each item before receiving that item's own benefits. Immediate effects resolve when triggered; 'after finishing' effects wait until the whole action is complete (including the Action-card move). Resolve simultaneous effects in the order chosen by the owning player. For Build II, take placement bonuses before the next building, while holding after-finishing bonuses until the entire Build action ends.
answers.evidence: X-tokens/general timing says earlier action bonuses may be used later and each item must be paid before its benefits. The summary defines after-finishing timing, Build II bonus order, and that the owner chooses simultaneous-effect order.

answers.answer: For each animal, check and meet all left-side conditions, pay its cost, house it legally, place its card, then resolve effects. A matching-continent partner zoo reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon on the animal card, so a double icon gives a 6-money reduction; you must still pay the full cost before any play-triggered money gain. Standard enclosures must be empty and meet the printed minimum size, then flip to occupied and normally hold one animal. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo, which holds at most three such animals. Reptiles and some birds may use their special enclosure if the required indicated spaces are available; mark those spaces with player tokens and do not flip the enclosure. Apply any water/rock adjacency requirements to the chosen housing; count distinct adjacent terrain hexes. Appeal and other ordinary effects resolve as specified on the card, with immediate effects before a second animal and after-finishing effects after the full Animals action and card movement.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action lists conditions, payment and the 3-money-per-continent-icon discount; standard/special enclosure admission and water/rock adjacency; and immediate versus after-finishing effect timing.

answers.answer: Animals II may play animal cards from display folders within reputation range, with an additional cost equal to the folder number; hand and display animals can be mixed, and the display is not replenished until turn end. At strength 5+, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies to that action. Animals II also allows animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: Animals II states display play within reputation range for folder-number additional cost, strength-5 reputation at the beginning, delayed refill, and upgrade-required conditions.

answers.answer: Existing animals may be moved only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, once for that building. Move all suitable animals that fit, choosing separately for each animal. Mark the number of special-enclosure spaces shown on each animal card with supply player tokens; the enclosure is never flipped. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all of that animal's requirements (including terrain); if none does, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size, flip none. The animal must fit the special enclosure's remaining capacity.
answers.evidence: Build II allows all suitable animals that fit to move immediately and only once per new Reptile House/Aviary. The special-enclosure and map clarification sections specify token capacity and the smallest-enclosure selection and fallback.

answers.answer: The four Association tasks have strengths 2 (increase reputation by 2), 3 (gain partner zoo), 4 (gain university), and 5 (conservation-project work). Association I performs exactly one task; Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total value is at most the action strength. Each task uses 1 active worker, but if you already have 1 worker on that task you must place 2; if 3 of your workers are already there, you cannot repeat it before the break. Other players' workers do not affect your task availability.
answers.evidence: Association section gives the task values and side-I/II limits, and says 1 worker is needed, 2 if one is already on the task, and no repeat after 3; opponents' workers do not matter.

answers.answer: Take partner zoos and universities from the Association board and put them on the lowest available spaces in their respective columns on your zoo map; take any printed space bonus immediately. You cannot take a duplicate university. Partner zoos must be from different continents and are limited to 4; the third and fourth require upgraded Association. Universities grant the reputation/research icons shown, and only a particular university raises the hand limit to 5 (otherwise it is 3, checked at breaks).
answers.evidence: Association tasks say tiles come from the Association board, go on the lowest available map spaces, and grant printed bonuses; duplicate universities are prohibited, partner limits/upgrades are stated, and universities include the hand-limit-five option.

answers.answer: Association I can play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately, or support a project already in play. Association II can also play the new project directly from the display within reputation range, paying the folder number. A support requires an unoccupied condition/reward level whose condition you fulfill; a level is blocked if any player's token is on it, and you may support a given project only once. Place one of your player tokens from the left edge of your zoo map on the chosen condition. The token's map bonus activates immediately, either before or after the project reward as you choose. New projects go above the Association board, pushing cards right; the display limit is 2/3/4 cards depending on player count. If one overflows, discard the rightmost project and return its tokens to their owners' supplies, not their zoo maps; activated bonuses remain activated.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work describes hand/display entry, support requirements and once limits, token source and bonus timing, and overflow discard/token destination.

answers.answer: No: the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement is matched to a size category, not an exact size: 2− accepts printed size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. On release, lose only that animal's printed Appeal before gaining conservation; discard the card and lose its icons. Retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated Appeal, and earlier effects already earned. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. To free space, first remove the animal's special-enclosure tokens if it could live there and such tokens can be removed; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or the smallest meeting size alone if none meets all requirements, or none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This also applies to flock animals.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild projects gives the size categories, losses/retained gains, new-project reputation distinction, and special-token/standard-enclosure fallback procedure.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand if action strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Sponsors II can play one or more cards if strength +1 is at least their summed levels (X-tokens can raise strength beyond 5); it can use hand cards or display cards within reputation range, paying each display card's folder number. Resolve cards one at a time, completing each card's instant effects (except after-finishing effects) before the next. Alternatively, Sponsors I advances the Break token by strength and pays that much money; you receive the full amount even if fewer spaces remain before the last space. Sponsors II's break-money option pays twice the amount.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action specifies side-I level/hand rules, side-II summed level budget and display cost, sequential resolution, and full or doubled break money.

answers.answer: Break steps: (1) discard down to hand limit (3, or 5 with the relevant university); (2) clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; (3) recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; (4) discard display folders 1 and 2, slide remaining cards down and refill; (5) take income: Appeal-track money, kiosk income, and break income on Sponsors and activated map bonuses; (6) reset the Break token. Each kiosk pays 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; an empty standard enclosure gives none, while an empty special enclosure does. If multiple players take display cards during break income, resolve them clockwise starting with the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), and refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure lists six steps and kiosk neighbors. It specifies clockwise display-card ordering and refilling between affected players during break income.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation points, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker; at 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token by that space (5 money remains available after tokens are gone); at 10, the first player to reach it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card. If nobody reaches 10 before game end, everyone discards one before end scoring. Check for game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or have passed one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger it. If triggered at a player's turn end, that player completes the turn and every other player takes one more turn; if triggered during a break, all players take one more turn. Each Final Scoring card can give at most 4 conservation points. For victory points, subtract the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter from your Appeal value. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player who supported more conservation projects, and if still tied the tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions states the 2/5/8/10 rewards, end-check timing and extra turns, the four-point Final Scoring cap, VP formula, positive-score condition and tiebreak.
